steps.title: Key Point
steps.body: Don't just write about one poem then the other. Weave them together - compare as you go.

steps.title: Why Alternating Works
steps.body: Examiners can see you're comparing throughout. It's easier to track similarities and differences. You cover both poems equally.

steps.title: Top Tip
steps.body: Comparison questions are typically worth 30 marks (AO1/AO2/AO3). Spend 45 minutes total: 5 mins planning your comparison points, 35 mins writing, 5 mins checking. Every paragraph must reference both poems — if you write a full paragraph on only one poem, you have already lost marks.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: What's the difference between alternating and integrated comparison? | Name three elements you should compare between poems. | Why should you include both similarities and differences?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Alternating: discuss one aspect, then compare both poems on it, then move to next aspect. Integrated: discuss both poems in every sentence. Alternating is clearer; integrated shows stronger comparison | Elements to compare: themes, methods (language/form/structure), tone, context, perspective, setting, imagery. | Both are required for a full comparison. Similarities show shared understanding; differences show nuanced analysis. A comparison that only lists similarities is incomplete.
